Class AToolBar

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
javax.swing.JToolBar
edu.cnu.mdi.graphics.toolbar.AToolBar
All Implemented Interfaces:
ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable, Accessible, SwingConstants
Direct Known Subclasses:
BaseToolBar
public abstract class AToolBar extends JToolBar
A convenience JToolBar for toolbars that contain a mutually exclusive set of JToggleButtons (i.e., a radio-button-like group), plus optional one-shot buttons.

This class manages:

  • a primary ButtonGroup that enforces mutual exclusivity
  • an optional default toggle button (selected when the active toggle is turned off)
  • a selection-change hook for subclasses
  • a registry of buttons by stable id for programmatic enable/disable

Button registry

Toolbars often need to enable/disable specific tools depending on application state (e.g., disable Delete when nothing is selected). Rather than forcing applications to keep references to every button instance, this class supports registering buttons under a stable string id and retrieving them later: 

toolBar.setButtonEnabled("delete", hasSelection);
toolBar.getButton("pointer", JToggleButton.class).setSelected(true);

For predefined buttons, you typically use ToolBits.getId(long) as the stable id. For application-defined buttons, choose your own ids.

Notes

  • You may still add non-toggle components (regular buttons, separators, etc.) using Container.add(Component) from JToolBar.
  • Only toggles added via addToggle(JToggleButton, boolean) are managed by the primary group.
  • The registry is populated by using the id-aware overloads addToggle(String, JToggleButton) / addButton(String, JButton). If you call Container.add(Component) directly, you may register manually via registerButton(String, AbstractButton).

  • Method Details

    • registerButton

      protected <T extends AbstractButton> T registerButton(String id, T button)
      Register a toolbar button under a stable id.

      This is used by the id-aware add methods. It is also safe for subclasses to call directly if they add components via Container.add(Component).

      For debugging and tooling, this method also sets:

      • Component.setName(String) to the id
      • button.putClientProperty("toolId", id)
      Parameters:
      id - stable identifier (non-blank).
      button - the button to register.
      Returns:
      the same button (for chaining).
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if id or button is null.
      IllegalArgumentException - if id is blank or already used by a different button.

    • removeButton

      public AbstractButton removeButton(String id)
      Remove a registered button from the registry by id.

      This does not remove the button from the Swing component hierarchy. If you dynamically remove tools, call this in addition to Container.remove(Component).

      Parameters:
      id - the id to remove (null/blank are ignored).
      Returns:
      the removed button, or null if none was registered.

    • requireButton

      public <T extends AbstractButton> T requireButton(String id, Class<T> type)
      Look up a registered toolbar button by id, throwing if missing.

      This is handy in application wiring code where missing tools should be a programming error rather than silently ignored.

      Type Parameters:
      T - type parameter.
      Parameters:
      id - registered id (non-blank).
      type - expected type.
      Returns:
      the typed button (never null).
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no button exists under that id, or the type is wrong.

    • registerExternalToggle

      public JToggleButton registerExternalToggle(String id, JToggleButton toggleButton)
      Registers an external toggle button with this toolbar's primary toggle group without adding the button to the toolbar component hierarchy.

      This is useful for palette buttons that should behave like tools and be mutually exclusive with toolbar toggles, while remaining visually located outside the toolbar.

      Parameters:
      id - stable identifier for the external tool
      toggleButton - external toggle button
      Returns:
      the same toggle button

      public void resetDefaultToggleButton()
